[01] The challenge

“[We were about to buy two more trucks with no idea if we could keep them busy.]”

[Client name] had grown on referrals and a busy summer. But leads came in waves: slammed in July, quiet in October. Three vendors ran ads, the website and the phones, and nobody could connect a call to a booked job. With two trucks on order, the owner needed demand they could plan around.

[02] Our approach, by Growth System stage

We worked on 3 of the 7 stages. The others were already in place or not part of this engagement.

  1. 1

    Strategy

    Not part of this engagement

  2. 2

    Build

    Not part of this engagement

  3. 3

    Generate

    Months 1–3

    Rebuilt Google Ads and Local Services Ads around booked jobs, not calls. Paused two campaigns that sent tune-up shoppers; added a maintenance-plan offer for the shoulder seasons.

    • Google Ads
    • LSA
    • Landing pages
  4. 4

    Convert

    Months 2–4

    Missed-call text-back in under 60 seconds, a 2-step follow-up for unbooked estimates, and a script for the CSR team. Calls now land in one inbox.

    • GHL
    • Call tracking
    • CSR script
  5. 5

    Measure

    Months 3–9

    One dashboard from call to booked job to invoice, connected to their field-service software, reviewed together every two weeks.

    • GHL reporting
    • ServiceTitan sync
    • Bi-weekly review

    Optimize

    Not part of this engagement

[04] What we learned

  • What worked

    Answering every call fast did more than any new campaign. Text-back alone recovered [~N] jobs a week.

  • What didn’t

    A Facebook test for tune-ups brought cheap leads that rarely booked. We stopped it after [N] weeks.

  • What we changed next

    Moved budget to maintenance plans before the fall, so October stayed busy for the first time.
